key_insight: InterMimicGen turns sparse human-object motion capture into a self-improving training loop for humanoid robots. By letting robot motion data and the tracking policy reinforce each other, it scales humanoid loco-manipulation beyond static imitation.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of large, executable humanoid loco-manipulation data. Human-object interaction captures are rich but sparse, inconsistent across sources, and difficult to directly retarget into robot motions that preserve whole-body and hand-object coordination.
method: Consolidate multiple motion-captured human-object interaction datasets into a unified collection.
Retarget human demonstrations into humanoid robot reference motions while preserving body coordination and dexterous manipulation.
Use a self-evolving loop where collected robot motion data improves the tracking policy, and the improved policy generates better motion data over time.
impact: This is useful for practitioners building humanoid control systems because it offers a scalable way to learn from real-world human interactions without requiring exhaustive hand-labeled robot demonstrations. It can accelerate data generation for locomotion-plus-manipulation tasks and improve policy robustness in complex embodied settings.

paper_title: InterMimicGen: Scaling Humanoid Loco-Manipulation through Self-Evolving Motion Imitation
paper_authors: Yucheng Zhang, Sirui Xu, Jinhong Li, Liuyu Bian, Anatulya Nandi
